title: Site Sets
appliesTo: how does an extension ship typoscript
welcome page instead of the site set
site set typoscript has no effect

hints.text: A site set is how a system extension ships TypoScript. It is a directory Configuration/Sets/<SetName>/ whose config.yaml carries a composer-style name ("typo3/fluid-styled-content"), an optional label, and an optional dependencies list naming other sets by that same name.
Next to config.yaml the set may hold setup.typoscript, settings.definitions.yaml, settings.yaml, labels.xlf and page.tsconfig. Only config.yaml is required.
A route-enhancers.yaml beside them is read as well, and what it declares is merged into the routing of every site that depends on the set.

Those enhancers merge rather than replace. SiteConfiguration folds each dependency's set into the last with ArrayUtility::replaceAndAppendScalarValuesRecursive(), in dependency order, and merges the site's own routeEnhancers over the result the same way. So a set adds one entry to an aspect's map inside an enhancer another set declared, and the identifier it declares under is a place in that tree rather than a name that wins.

A fragment is therefore only whole while the set that declares the rest is a dependency. Drop that dependency and what reaches the router is the fragment alone: EnhancerFactory refuses it with exception 1537298284, "Enhancer type cannot be empty", and every request of the site answers HTTP 500. Nothing in the route-enhancers.yaml says which set it is completing, so the dependency is what carries that and the file cannot be read without it.

A key config.yaml carries that SetDefinition has no parameter for is fatal rather than ignored. YamlSetDefinitionProvider::createDefinition() spreads the parsed file into that readonly constructor, so PHP's \Error comes back as InvalidSetException whose message ends in "Invalid properties: <key>". The set is then dropped and every site depending on it answers HTTP 500, so one stray key in one set is a whole frontend down rather than one feature missing. SetDefinition's constructor is the list of what may be written, and the files above are how the longer values arrive.

The routes key stays with the site and no set can carry one. A static route — robots.txt, a text file, an asset, a page rendered to a fixed path — is an entry under routes in config/sites/<identifier>/config.yaml, which the StaticRouteResolver middleware answers from before the page is resolved.

A site takes a set up by naming it under dependencies in its own config/sites/<identifier>/config.yaml. The key is spelled dependencies and nothing in that file is called sets, while the accessor is Site::getSets() — so the one relationship is asked for under one word and read under another.

The site entity's other sources are keyed the same way. The settings key of that config.yaml becomes Site::getSettings(), and the site's own TypoScript and page TSconfig come from setup.typoscript, constants.typoscript and page.tsconfig lying beside config.yaml rather than from any key in it.

A site naming a set, or holding a setup.typoscript, constants.typoscript or page.tsconfig of its own, is a TypoScript root: its frontend renders without a sys_template record on the root page. A site with none of them and no such record errors out instead of rendering. Site::isTypoScriptRoot() is the core's own test for that: the dependencies list is not empty, or one of those files sits beside config.yaml. It is @internal, so core code and a core functional test call it and everything else reads it as the description of when that record can go.

hints: This is how an extension ships TypoScript, and a project's own sitepackage is an extension like any other — the mechanism does not change because the repository is not the core's. Configuring one installation is where it stops being a convention and becomes that site's decision, and this server does not make it.

hints.text: What a set contributes is overridden by what the installation was created with: typo3 setup --create-site leaves a welcome page object behind that is read after every set, and installation-setup says where that object sits on each major and how to be rid of it.

hints: site-set-settings is what replaces constants, and it is why a site's own values are kept in one place: settings.yaml and the inline settings key are alternatives rather than layers, so the first backend save drops what was written inline. site-set-labels-and-layouts is what a set declares beside TypoScript, and a page layout column it ships without an identifier is a column the frontend template cannot reach. site-set-migration is the registration the move leaves behind in ext_localconf.php, which nothing reports and no scanner sees. development-installation-page-object is where a set carrying a page object comes from at all, for a package that ships none and still has to be looked at in a browser.

title: Site Set Settings Instead of TypoScript Constants

hints.text: settings.definitions.yaml is where a set declares its settings: a categories map and a settings map, each entry with default, type and category. It is the replacement for TypoScript constants — reaching for constants.typoscript in new code is the mistake to avoid here.

A settings value is addressed by its dotted path, and both spellings of it resolve: the set's own settings.yaml writes a nested tree, and the site's config.yaml or a test fixture may hand the same thing over as flat dotted keys — 'my_ext.products.requestPage' => 4 — because SiteSettings flattens a tree into those keys itself and reads either. So the nested form in the set is a convention rather than a requirement.

A site's config/sites/<identifier>/settings.yaml and the settings key inline in its config.yaml are alternatives, not layers: when settings.yaml exists, TYPO3 uses it wholesale and does not merge the inline values into it. Set defaults sit below whichever site-local source wins. The backend settings editor persists to settings.yaml, so keep a site's own values in one place or the first backend save can silently leave inline values behind.

title: Labels and Page Layouts a Site Set Ships

hints.text: The set's labels.xlf resolves to the translation domain <ext>.sets.<setname>; typo3_translation_domain_lookup computes it from the path.
The set's labels.xlf is picked up from the set's own directory and there is no domain to address it by: a label of the set is referenced with its full LLL:EXT: path.

A page layout the set ships in page.tsconfig declares its columns under mod.web_layout.BackendLayouts, and every column needs an explicit `identifier`: that identifier is what the frontend template addresses as {content.<identifier>}. Leaving it out is accepted where a generated identifier still stands in and refused where it does not, and no template can name that column either way — page-content-areas has what each of the two costs.

title: What Moving TypoScript Into a Set Leaves Behind
hints: ExtensionManagementUtility::addTypoScriptSetup() and addStaticFile() are the predecessor and are still called from a few sysexts, addTypoScriptSetup with an includeInSiteSets flag that folds the content into the set mechanism. Both mechanisms coexist; new code ships a set.

hints.text: Moving an extension's TypoScript into a set leaves what registered the old static include behind in ext_localconf.php, and nothing reports it. A $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['FE']['contentRenderingTemplates'] entry naming the removed Configuration/TypoScript/ path can no longer be matched by anything, so it is a cleanup rather than a defect — the content-rendering-templates hint says what reads that key and what a matched entry would have done.
Site set resolution is covered by functional tests under typo3/sysext/core/Tests/Functional/Site/Set/; the labels have their own check, checkIntegritySetLabels.
